title: Contarini: our inherent justice is inchoate and imperfect
source_text: XXX. Atque hi quidem loquuntur ac docent rigidiores ex Pontificiis. Sed qui sunt inter eos aequiores, rotunde, simpliciter, & aperte fatentur justitiam quae nobis inhaeret tenuem, inchoatam, & imperfectam esse. Quo de numero in primis est Cardinalis Con-tarenus: is enim Tractatu de Justificatione, anno 72. superioris saeculi, post Conci-lium Tridentinum edito; idque cum approbatione Doctorum regentium Theologicae facultatis Parisiensis, clare & expresse docet & inculcat justitiae fidelibus inhaerentis im-perfectionem. Haec nostra justitia, inquit, est inchoata & imperfecta, quae tueri nos non potest quin in multis offendamus, quin assidue peccemus.
pass_a_gloss: And these indeed are the way of speaking and teaching of the more rigid among the Papists. But those among them who are fairer roundly, simply, and openly confess that the righteousness which inheres in us is thin, begun, and imperfect. Of which number first is Cardinal Contarini: for he, in the Treatise on Justification published in the seventy-second year of the previous century after the Council of Trent, and that with the approval of the doctors regent of the Theological faculty of Paris, clearly and expressly teaches and inculcates the imperfection of the righteousness inherent in believers. This our righteousness, he says, is begun and imperfect, which cannot protect us from offending in many things, from continually sinning.
pass_b_english: Milder Romans (Contarini, Paris-approved) frankly call inherent justice inchoate and imperfect.
It cannot keep us from often offending.

choices.why: Key lemma for De Justitia densify §1064.
